summary: The aim is right: keep source controls in the documentary occurrence and keep word homes plain. The proposed mechanism is broader than needed, though. It adds a second parts library inside canonical_home that would repeat guards canonical_parts already has. It also leaves two validators that still reject what it needs: validate_occurrences rejects a canonical pointer that keeps its own conditions, and validate_redirection rejects redirecting a segment that has conditions. A safer, smaller design keeps every word home strict and relaxes only the occurrence side, for an explicit short whitelist of segment controls. If you still choose the canonical_home extension, it is acceptable only with the constraints below.
required_constraints: Word homes never contain controls. Do not filter a host's controls out at generation time. Put the plain words in an existing pure host (canonical_parts, or a plain canonical_home), and keep the controls on the occurrence segment that points to it.

Segment controls allowed on a canonical occurrence segment: conditions, condition_instruction, condition_instruction_language, speaker. All others stay rejected, in particular condition_end_corresp, marked, instructions, edition_label, deferred_page_boundary, repeat, repeat_cue, transclude, anchor, language, source_reference_part and corresp/source*. condition_end_corresp cannot work: unit_document finds the scope end by matching candidate['corresp'], and corresp has been removed from a pointer segment. Segment-level marked needs parentheses removed in both the fidelity check and the attestation check (build.py:431-436 removes them only in the output), so leave it out until a real case needs it. ushenei_seirim is not marked.

Unit-level controls (conditions, marked, instructions, head, opening_page) are already legal on ordinary occurrence units that use canonical pointers. Nothing new is needed for them. poetry stays rejected: a prose home would lose the source's lines. Citations on an occurrence must not target a part identity, otherwise one printing's citation follows the shared words into every caller. Allow citation targets only on the occurrence/context URN.

The literal attestation stays exact: scan, printed_page and raw text must match what validate_occurrences already requires. Each canonical segment keeps exactly one plain fragment. Multi-page parts such as AlKen keep using context='literal'.

The library or home root URN can never be addressed: map_root=false and omit_publication_urn=true, and check_target must reject it in reuse, repeat, transclude, repeat_cue, citations, source_order and expanded_order references. canonical_parts already does this through pure_roots. If you keep the canonical_home extension, add contextual home URNs to that same set (realizations.py:273-311). Today only canonical_parts roots are rejected there.

Parts are never ranges: keep the 'Noncontiguous canonical parts cannot be a range' rule. Uminchatam becomes two pointers (offering_formula/text, and offering_formula/ushenei_seirim inside its own rite conditional), not one range.

The generated XML scope of each part must equal its segment-based canonical_text. The checker compares segments (_range_segments), but the compiler resolves milestone scopes. Every home part must close where its segment ends (end_reference=True, or the next same-unit milestone). This is the real reason Aleinu needs end_reference=True.

Aleinu's end_reference=True does change what urn:...musaf/aleinu/text resolves to: the Deut 4:39 quotation leaves its scope. Apply it to he and en together. Before accepting it, list every repeat, transclude, canonical, reuse, order reference and citation that names aleinu/text, and require each caller's literal text either to exclude the verse or to switch to a range ending at .../veyadata/deuteronomy_4/39.

validate_redirection (baseline.py:38-83) remains the gate for re-pointing the accepted witnesses. Relax its segment.get('conditions') rejection only for the whitelisted controls, and only because they stay on the occurrence pointer. Still reject source_reference_part, condition_end_corresp, multiple fragments and every fragment interpretation.

Accepted witnesses change only in UNIT_MAPPING_FIELDS and SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS (canonical, canonical_end, corresp, source, end_reference, and canonical_home if used). validate_baseline must pass with an unchanged baseline file.

Callers of a part that came from a conditioned or speaker-marked printing must bear their own source condition and speaker. At minimum, bind the stripped host controls into each caller's realization payload so review sees them. Preferably also fail if the caller has no condition on the same fs type and feature names. Do not add any override or bypass field.
Root URNs for a new library or home must already be registered. build.py:1171-1207 validates unit['urn'] and canonical_home.urn against the registry even though neither is emitted.
No repeat or transclude workaround anywhere. Existing tests that expect strict hosts to reject non-plain segments must still fail.

risks: Validation is green but the scope is wrong: segment-based canonical_text can match while the compiled milestone scope (for example aleinu/text running through Deut 4:39) duplicates or drops words in callers.

Moving rubrics into the home: if a stripped condition rubric, speaker or citation reached the home, it would print in every caller. A stripped rite condition (ushenei_seirim, frankfurt_am_main=false) would make the words unconditional in callers that forget their own condition, and an undefined rite would then print both alternatives with no rubric.
Parentheses of a marked passage leaking into the home words, or a fidelity mismatch, if segment-level marked is allowed without removing them in the checks.

Page breaks: home pages are forced to page_start=false. Context page breaks come from the pointer fragment's scan/page_start and, for a conditioned segment, from build.py:392 before the conditional. head and opening_page in the home would emit a pb without a fragment, so they must stay in the occurrence.
Root exposure: a canonical_home with map_root=false still writes a publication idno unless omit_publication_urn is set, and check_target does not protect canonical_home URNs today.
Receipt gap: a caller's fidelity hash covers only words, so a change to host controls does not invalidate callers. Host review is invalidated, through the witness and the baseline.
Two parts libraries (canonical_parts and contextual canonical_home) with different guards would drift apart over time.
Aleinu end_reference changes what an existing published URN resolves to, not only metadata. Existing callers can silently lose the verse.

If a home were filtered, canonical_text, _range_segments, review_payloads and validate_generated would all need the same filtered view. One missed call means the review hash would no longer match the output.
recommended_minimal_change: Do not add contextual_controls to canonical_home. (1) Put the plain words in canonical_parts libraries using the existing identities: yismechu/text, offering_formula/text, offering_formula/ushenei_seirim, offering_formula/useir_lekhapper/text. Each library copies its attesting fragment exactly. (2) Re-point the accepted witnesses with mapping fields only (canonical instead of corresp/source), gated by validate_redirection. Unit-level conditions, marked and instructions stay as they are on the occurrence. (3) Code change: in validate_occurrences, allow the set {conditions, condition_instruction, condition_instruction_language, speaker} on a canonical occurrence segment. In validate_redirection, allow conditions only under that same whitelist. Change nothing else, because build.py already emits a conditional and speaker around the pointer correctly. (4) Bind the stripped or adjacent occurrence controls of each part's attesting witness into each caller's realization payload. (5) New repeated occurrences point to the parts and select their source-specific pointing through wording_variants on the library host, keeping their own conditions. (6) Numbers 28/9-10 and 29/1-2: use the existing plain hosts plus overlays; their citations are outside canonical_text. (7) AlKen: existing context='literal' home. (8) Aleinu: end_reference=True in he and en after the caller audit above.
tests_required: Strict-host regression: a canonical_home or canonical_parts host with conditions, marked, speaker or citations still raises, and validate_pure_parts still rejects any non-plain key.

Occurrence whitelist: a canonical segment with conditions, condition_instruction or speaker passes; condition_end_corresp, marked, instructions, repeat, transclude, source_reference_part, corresp, two or more fragments, or any fragment interpretation still raises.
validate_redirection: ushenei_seirim passes only with the whitelisted controls kept on the pointer; it still rejects multi-fragment segments, quotations, alternatives and source_reference_part.
Baseline: validate_baseline passes against the unchanged accepted baseline after re-pointing; changing any protected byte (fragment text, conditions, instructions) fails.

Root safety: library or home URNs as the target of a reuse, repeat, transclude, repeat_cue, citation, or source/expanded order reference raise; no idno, no div corresp, and no duplicate old or new root in the generated files.

Compiler projection (actual compile, not validator only), Yismechu context: holiday-aggregate shabbat unknown gives the marked rubric plus the words, true gives the words without the rubric, false gives nothing. The library words appear exactly once per project.

Compiler projection, Uminchatam plus Frankfurt with rite unknown, frankfurt_am_main=true and frankfurt_am_main=false: exact word sequences, the Frankfurt rubric only when unknown, and offering_formula/text kept in all three.

Scope fidelity: for every part identity, the text resolved from the generated XML scope equals canonical_text, whitespace-normalized, for he and en. Covers the Aleinu end_reference case, with a negative test showing the old scope fails.
Aleinu caller audit test: every existing reference to aleinu/text still matches its literal reading after end_reference.
Source and expanded aligned exact words: he/en parallel alignment boundaries unchanged at the occurrence; the expanded order is word-identical to the documentary order for each condition setting.

Wording overlays: a new occurrence choosing a non-first pointing variant must declare every option; mismatched or partial selection raises; the generated caller declare/endDeclare is local to the transclusion.

Page breaks: the context keeps the exact pb n/facs positions (including a conditioned segment starting on a new page); the library or home contains no pb; AlKen literal context pb positions unchanged.

Receipts: changing a host or occurrence control makes its realization review stale; changing library words makes every caller's fidelity hash stale; the caller payload includes the bound adjacent controls.
Stale-file check: no duplicate generated publication URN, and no file left over from a previous canonical home layout.
better_existing_interface_if_available: canonical_parts (validate_pure_parts, prepare_unit forcing map_root=false, omit_publication_urn=true and page_start=false, the literal-attestation check, pure_roots/pure_ids target guards, and validate_generated's no-pb/no-note/no-conditional check) is already the non-addressable library with only part URNs and no controls that the proposal describes. Use it together with mapping-only redirection through baseline.validate_redirection. The only gap is occurrence-side support for segment-level conditions, condition_instruction and speaker, which build.unit_document already renders around inline canonical pointers. Keep canonical_home context='literal' for multi-page AlKen and the existing plain hosts for Numbers 28-29.
